title: GROUP BY, HAVING & Aggregates in SQL

scenes.line1: How do you summarize data in SQL?
scenes.say: How do you summarize and filter groups of data in SQL? Should you use GROUP BY or HAVING?

scenes.label: GROUP BY
scenes.sub: Groups rows by column values for analysis
scenes.say: GROUP BY lets you group rows by column values, so you can analyze each group separately.

rows.b: Adds up values in a group

scenes.say: Aggregate functions like count, sum, and average operate on each group to summarize your data.
Remember: WHERE filters rows before grouping. HAVING filters groups after aggregation.

scenes.title: Departments with 10+ employees
scenes.say: Here's how you find departments with more than ten employees using GROUP BY and HAVING.

scenes.question: Where do you filter on aggregates?
scenes.right: Use HAVING with COUNT(*) > 10, not WHERE.
scenes.say: Interview trap: You can't use WHERE to filter on aggregate results like count. Use HAVING instead.
